findings.title: New feature changes `--features` help output but approved help snapshots are not updated
findings.body: Adding `ROLLING_UPDATES` adds `rolling-updates[:v1]` to the 'Possible values' list that the `--features` option prints in CLI help. That list is checked by the approval-based help tests (`HelpCommandDistTest.*.approved.txt` for start, start-dev, build, export, import, update-compatibility, etc.). None of those snapshot files are part of this PR, so the help tests are likely to fail once this merges. Regenerate and commit the approved help files together with the new feature.

findings.title: Operator doc says the Operator will fail without `rolling-updates`, but nothing enforces this
findings.body:
The new CAUTION block says the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled or 'the Keycloak Operator will fail'. This PR adds no Operator code that checks the feature. The existing `Recreate` strategy behaves the same whether or not the feature is on.

The default `<not set>` strategy also clearly works without the feature: `UpgradeTest` runs the `null` strategy case without enabling it. The statement is therefore inaccurate at this commit. Readers will also be confused about whether the feature is needed when they don't set `update.strategy`.

Either add Operator-side validation that reports a clear status error, or reword the doc to say exactly when the feature is needed and what happens without it.

findings.title: Hard-coded `--features=rolling-updates` in the command template can clobber the user's real feature set
findings.body:
The `updatecompatibility` macro now appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every documented `update-compatibility` invocation. The same guide tells users to pass exactly the options used by `start`.

Users who already run with `--features=<their list>` will now pass a second `--features` value that replaces their list. The metadata/check then runs with a different feature set than the real deployment, or the duplicate option causes a CLI error. Users need to add `rolling-updates` to their existing list, not override it.

Separately, `features` is a build-time option. With an optimized (`--optimized`) image, passing it at runtime does not take effect. The commands will then exit with code 4 unless the image was rebuilt with the feature, which is why `Dockerfile-custom-image` had to be changed. Neither point is documented.

findings.title: Feature-disabled test checks neither the new exit code nor the `check` subcommand
findings.body:
`testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text for the `metadata` subcommand. The PR's main contract change is the new exit code `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (and the move of `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3), and scripts are told to rely on these exit codes.

No test asserts that a disabled feature yields exit code 4, that `check` is also gated, or that an incompatible result now returns 3. A regression in the exit codes would go unnoticed. Add `assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED, result.exitCode())` for both subcommands, and assert 3 in `testWrongVersions`.
